simple.meaning: בָּכַר (bâkar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to give the birthright.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 27:26. The surrounding contexts include birth, family line, firstborn.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּכַר (H1069) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּכַר (bâkar) / H1069 is traced through Leviticus 27:26, Deuteronomy 21:16, Jeremiah 4:31, Ezekiel 47:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.usage: make firstborn, be firstling, bring forth first child (new fruit).
definitions.full: H1069. bakar [ בָּכַר ] verb (Late Hebrew בְּכֵּר , Aramaic בַּכֵּר , ; compare Arabic rise early, do anything early ; , virgin, woman having her first child ; Ethiopic primogenitus ; Assyrian bukru , first-born , Dl § 65, 5 ) — Pi`el Imperfect יְבַכֵּר Ezek 47:12 ; Infinitive לְבַכֵּר Deut 21:16 ; — 1 bear early, new fruit Ezek 47:12 . 2 make or constitute as first-born Deut 21:16 (denominative of בכיר ). Pu`al Imperfect יְבֻכַּר Lev 27:26 born or made a firstling . Hiph`il Participle f. מַבְכִּירָה Jer 4:31 one bearing her first child .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; properly, to burst the womb, i.e. (causatively) bear or make early fruit (of woman or tree); also (as denominative from 1061 )

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘However the firstborn among animals, which belongs to Yahweh as a firstborn, no man may dedicate, whether an ox or a sheep. It is Yahweh’s.

then it shall be, in the day that he causes his sons to inherit that which he has, that he may not give the son of the beloved the rights of the firstborn before the son of the hated, who is the firstborn;

For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her who gives birth to her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, who gasps for breath, who spreads her hands, saying, “Woe is me now! For my soul faints before the murderers.”

By the river on its bank, on this side and on that side, will grow every tree for food, whose leaf won’t wither, neither will its fruit fail. It will produce new fruit every month, because its waters issue out of the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaf for healing.”
